source: So be it, then. If he asks, then I shall grant it.
I... I only ever suspected Claudius. And never out loud. I never knew he was capable of such a thing.
My son, I swear to you I never knew. I swear it.
Dry your eyes, Mother. I'm going to get revenge. For both of us.
You'll see soon enough. For now, speak none of this to my uncle. I'll handle the rest.
Time to lug this poor old fool's corpse.
Hamlet! Stop!
Oh, my God.
This evil woman!
Please, Hamlet, don't do this!
My son-- My son-- No...
I should have killed you the moment I suspected you helped that snake Claudius with his foul deeds!
Were it up to me, you'd die a death a thousand times more painful than what you're about to suffer!
Hamlet. Get on the ground immediately. Stand down.
You cannot stop me. Not now. I refuse to stand down.
He's just unconscious, my lady.
What about you, my Queen? Are you...
Bernardo... My son. What's wrong with him?
He's not in his right mind. He's not himself.
I'll have to let the King know what has happened here.
I'm not letting you throw me in some filthy cell for avenging my father's death.
No—! No, Hamlet—!
My son, you fool...
This is wretched.
I'm sorry, my lady.
And to you, Hamlet.
Close his eyes. I can't see him like that.
I'll remove him, my lady.
Warm yourself by the fire, please. And turn away. Don't look at this gruesome scene.
Leave it to me. Hamlet was one of my oldest, most beloved friends. I will clean what remains.
You murderous, traitorous woman. You owe my father's honor your life.
I love you with all my heart. Please don't let it come to this.
Now, good riddance to a traitorous woman.
My little baby boy...
N-No, please, no...
This can't be happening.
Why did it have to come to this? Why?
There's no longer any reason for me to be here.
My son is dead, and I...
Nothing on this earth matters anymore. All good and beloved things are dust.
Come, blade. Find your noble resting place.
Holy Father, grant me a Heaven set before this evil summer began.
One where the people I loved are still alive.
My lady, His Majesty wishes to speak with you.
(Goodness. What now?)
Lady Ophelia.
My deepest condolences again about your father. He was an incredible man.
Thank you, my lord. What is this about?
Earlier, you mentioned something to me about a voyage at sea.
You told me I would be unsuccessful in sending Hamlet to his demise.
You knew this long before I myself even formed this thought. And yet, you told no one.
Am I to understand that your secrecy is a tacit approval?
What of it if so, my lord?
I understand my nephew has caused you no small amount of pain.
You may be interested to hear this: I plan to give Rosencrantz and Guildenstern a letter to deliver to the Queen of England.
You may be interested to hear this: I plan to give the crew of this ship a letter to deliver to the Queen of England.
And within that letter is writ my nephew's death warrant, a request to have him quietly executed.
I have faith that my letter will reach its intended audience safely. Even so...
As far as I know, you are the only one who knows my true intentions. I shall not be telling anyone else about what the letter itself contains.
If you wish to avail yourself to a King, and so earn my personal favor, perhaps you can join Hamlet on his journey. Ensure he does not make it back.
The ship sails at ten in the morning. Go with him, and do my bidding. Make sure Hamlet dies, and you will be justly rewarded.
Well? What happened?
I was hiding for ages!
Do you know how hungry I was? I nearly gnawed my own leg off!
I'm sorry, Guilda. I forgot to tell Rosencrantz.
You forgot? Well, remember this: That's the last fake funeral I'll ever ask you to plan!
I'm sorry, Guilda. I told Rosencrantz, but I guess there just wasn't enough time.
Not enough time? Well, remember this: That's the last fake funeral I'll ever ask you to plan!
Probably for the best.
Now I've got to go explain to Rosie all about my prank. She's going to be angry.
Oops. She's here.
You're not... dead.
Rosie. I can explain.
I don't care. I don't need to know.
Just never do that to me again.
Do you know how awful that felt? How frightened I was?
I never want to feel that way. Not ever again.
Sorry, Rosie.
I thought it'd be funny. I really did.
Oh, Guilda, my peach.
Having you around is the only part which makes life funny.
Without you, I don't quite know that there's a point to any of it at all.
I'll give you two some time alone.
My thanks, Ophelia.
There's nothing that can be done now.
Hamlet must be separated from us. From everyone.
For the safety of those around him, and of himself.
Lady Rosencrantz, Lady Guildenstern, I'm ordering you to go to England with him.
I might point out, my lord, that just a moment ago we were sitting in your dungeon, accused of treason.
Rosie! What's that saying? Never look a gift horse in the mouth! They're a particularly aggressive breed!
A gift horse isn't a breed of horse, Guilda.
Are you going to be the one to tell the gift horse that? It'll bite your face off!
What? What's this got to do with biting? I... Oh, dear. Allow me to explain the saying.
Yes, sir!
Just looking at the two of you gives me a headache. Nevertheless, my options are limited here. You shall go with Hamlet to England.
If you can do this for me, then I shall lift all accusations of treason against you.
So... we aren't going to be executed and we get a free vacation to England. Today might be the best day of my life.
In exchange, I ask a simple favor.
When there, make sure to deliver this letter to the Queen.
She will prescribe a fitting treatment for Hamlet.
Something to lift his spirits for good?
In a manner of speaking.
My lord, we've been informed that we may be in grave danger if we board a ship to England.
And after that last fortune-teller told me my hands would swell up in the bath, I'm a believer.
But they always do t--
Bah. Never mind.
My good lady, have you not learned to distrust those who claim to know the future?
Well, this time it wasn't a fortune-teller. It was Lady Ophelia! I trust her even more!
Lady Ophelia?
(Curse that girl.)
Where—how—could she have heard something like that?
At any rate, please let me clarify. You are going to England. I will aim to make your journey both a comfortable and safe one.
And please, don't take further advice from Lady Ophelia. She's deeply, deeply unwell as of late.
Hamlet's gone nutters. Can't blame you.
Hush, Guilda. For God's sake. A man is dead. Can't we be appropriate?
Hush, Guilda. For God's sake. His father died. Can't we be appropriate?
Fine. I suppose so.
Off you go, my good ladies. The ship sails soon.
Rosencrantz? Guildenstern? Why are you here? I thought--
All a misunderstanding, my good nephew. And I am to blame.
What I initially believed to be treason, I now realize was a momentary error in judgement on my part.
As a result, the good Lady Rosencrantz and Lady Guildenstern are here to accompany you on your voyage to England.
Not to mention your uncle forced us to make him a secret promise!
--Errrr, what Guilda means is, we made a secret promise that we would take utmost care of you on this journey!
(Guilda, you dolt.)
Right. Yes. Exactly what she said.
So. It's time we bid goodbye to Denmark once and for all.
This will be good for you, Hamlet.
It'll be just like the old days again!
We'll be running through London, in and out of trouble...
All the diplomatic immunity, none of the down sides!
When you say it like that, it sounds almost like this isn't a banishment.
But let us all make no mistake. My uncle is sending this monster where I cannot cause further harm.
Farewell, my dearest nephew.
May your journey be swift and uneventful, and may you be delivered quickly to England's arms.
Terribly poetic of you.
Ah. You're here, Ophelia.
What's all this? Where are you going?
I'm now away to England, perhaps never to return. I hesitate to even ask if you'll think of me. If you'll miss me.
Ah, Hamlet. There's been a change in plans.
Ophelia's going to join you aboard the ship!
Yes, Hamlet. I've been tasked with escorting you.
In these troubled times... Claudius felt it would be best for you to have a familiar face close by.
Perhaps... so.
Be off, then. The both of you. The wind is getting stronger each moment.
Bon voyage, beloveds. Take care.
My father is dead because of you. I can't say I will.
I cannot blame you.
Know only that, for whatever an idiot's word is worth, I'm sorry.
I never meant to kill him.
That's an unfair question, isn't it?
Mm. I suppose it is.
For whatever little it's worth, I'm sorry about all that happened with your father. I truly am.
To England! Farewell for now, Hamlet.
For now, perhaps for ever.
Hamlet. Why so dismal? This is our chance to embark on a new adventure!
Yes, a new life, a new journey—in England!
Let's be off. I sense a storm coming on.
Well, looks like it's time for me to depart.
This castle has been good to me these long few years.
But fairer places await!
I can imagine the ship waiting out in harbor now.
I always dreamed one of these ships might sail for me.
Your trunks have been loaded, my lord. Shall we board the longboat?
Yes, I think that appropriate, Reynaldo.
Goodbye, you loon. Don't dig yourself into a hole too deep.
I'll miss you too, Brit.
You ought to be off while the winds are good.
Yes, yes, the winds will go, and so must we.
Goodbye, sister. Be safe.
Goodbye, everyone.
To Paris, then!
ERROR: If you're seeing this text, something has gone very wrong!
Bartender, a flagon of the finest, if you please.
You must be that one they call Othello.
...So it would seem. And you must be the one they call Lord Laertes.
Lord Laertes... it always was a funny title. I suppose I am now a Duke, aren't I?
Unfortunate news about your father, m'lord.
He was a good man. The best sort of man, a stalwart advisor, and a wonderful father.
What sad luck that our ship was delayed in its leave of harbor.
I was presented with a letter the moment I stepped ashore here...
